findings.summary: The note says work before the savepoint is 'still committed', but that work is only kept in the open transaction and becomes permanent at COMMIT.
findings.evidence: work before sp1 is still committed
findings.fix: Reword to 'work before sp1 is kept and becomes permanent at COMMIT'. If the transaction later rolled back fully, that earlier work would be undone too.

findings.summary: The lost-update fix bullet holds two alternatives in one line, and the code that follows only shows one of them.
findings.evidence: Fix: lock the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or use one atomic UPDATE
findings.fix: Split into two bullets, one for the lock and one for the atomic UPDATE. Show a one-line atomic UPDATE example alongside the locking code.

findings.summary: The REPEATABLE READ bullet mixes the snapshot rule with InnoDB-specific gap-lock behaviour, so the page holds two ideas in one bullet and reads as if it contradicts the table's 'yes (standard)' phantom entry.
findings.evidence: REPEATABLE READ: one snapshot from the first read / InnoDB adds gap locks, blocking most phantoms
findings.fix: Make the InnoDB gap-lock note its own labelled bullet, 'MySQL InnoDB only: gap locks block most phantoms'. Keep the snapshot bullet limited to the standard behaviour.

findings.summary: The setting-the-level bullet packs three ideas into one line: per-transaction scope, order differing by database, and a MySQL error code.
findings.evidence: Set it per transaction; the order differs by database, and MySQL gives ERROR 1568 if it is wrong
findings.fix: Split into three bullets: set per transaction, PostgreSQL order, MySQL order and ERROR 1568. Put each rule before its matching code block.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet's isolation table drops the READ UNCOMMITTED row and the dirty-read column, so it is incomplete compared with page 4.
findings.evidence: Level | Non-repeatable | Phantom / READ COMMITTED | allowed | allowed
findings.fix: Add a Dirty column and the READ UNCOMMITTED row, or copy the page 4 table.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet's command code block runs SAVEPOINT and ROLLBACK TO together with no stated purpose, and the PostgreSQL/MySQL ordering note sits apart from the line it applies to.
findings.fix: Add a one-line idea before the code: 'savepoint = partial undo inside a transaction'. Keep the ordering note directly beside the SET TRANSACTION line.
